title: Introduction to the Seerah and the Era of Jahiliyyah
overview: This lecture introduces the spiritual and practical benefits of studying the Seerah of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, emphasizing its role in understanding the Quran and increasing faith. The speaker explores the ancient history of Makkah, from the settlement of Ibrahim and Ismail to the eventual corruption of pure monotheism into the idol worship of the Jahiliyyah period.
lessons: The humanity of the Prophet ﷺ is a mercy; it proves that his exemplary character and obedience are achievable for all human beings.
True faith (Iman) is incomplete without prioritizing the love of the Prophet ﷺ over all worldly relations.
Hajar’s story is a profound lesson in tawakkul (reliance on Allah); when one acts for Allah's sake, He provides from sources unimaginable.
Religious corruption often starts with charismatic but misguided leaders who introduce innovations into pure worship, as seen with Amr ibn Luhayy.
Knowledge of historical context (asbab al-nuzul) is a vital tool for preventing the misinterpretation of Quranic verses.

chapters.title: Benefits of Studying the Seerah
chapters.summary: The episode begins by outlining why studying the life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is essential for every Muslim. The speaker explains that following a human messenger, rather than an angel, provides believers with a practical and achievable example to emulate. Studying the Seerah acts as a boost to faith (Iman) and fosters a deep love for the Prophet ﷺ, which is a fundamental requirement of Islamic belief. Furthermore, the character of the Prophet ﷺ is described as the living implementation of the Quran.
key_points: Following a human messenger removes the excuse that his example is impossible to emulate.
Love for the Prophet ﷺ is a prerequisite for complete Iman.
Aishah (RA) described the Prophet's character as the Quran in practice.
Studying the Seerah increases respect for the Prophet ﷺ even among non-Muslims.

chapters.title: Understanding Revelation through Context
chapters.summary: This section explains the importance of asbab al-nuzul, or the reasons for revelation, in understanding the Quran. The speaker provides the example of the Prophet’s uncle, Abu Talib, who protected his nephew from the Quraysh but died without accepting Islam. This context is vital to understanding the verse that states the Prophet ﷺ cannot guide whom he loves, as only Allah grants guidance. Without this historical background, the gravity and depth of certain Quranic verses would remain hidden to the reader.
key_points: Asbab al-nuzul (reasons for revelation) is a science within the study of Seerah.
Abu Talib served as a shield for the Prophet ﷺ during the Meccan period.
The verse 'Surely you do not guide whom you love' was revealed regarding Abu Talib's death.
Abu Jahl and other leaders of the Quraysh influenced Abu Talib to die on his ancestral religion.

chapters.title: The Foundations of Meccan Civilization
chapters.summary: To understand the society the Prophet ﷺ was born into, the speaker traces the history of Makkah back to Ibrahim and Ismail (alayhimas-salam). Following Allah's command, Ibrahim left Hajar and baby Ismail in a barren, uninhabited valley. This act of absolute trust (tawakkul) was rewarded with the miracle of the Zamzam well, which gushed forth after the angel Jibril hit the ground. The presence of water attracted the noble tribe of Jurhum from Yemen, marking the first settlement in Makkah.
key_points: Ibrahim is known as Abu al-Anbiya because all subsequent prophets came from his lineage.
Makkah is described in the Quran as a valley without agriculture or vegetation.
The Zamzam well was revealed through the angel Jibril for Hajar and Ismail.
The tribe of Jurhum were the first to settle Makkah after the discovery of Zamzam.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Ka'bah and the Call to Hajj
chapters.summary: Ibrahim and Ismail (alayhimas-salam) rebuilt the Ka'bah on the foundations originally established by Adam (alayhis-salam). During construction, Ibrahim used the Black Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad), which was sent from Allah and was originally white. The speaker describes Maqam Ibrahim as the station from which Ibrahim oversaw the work to ensure it was straight. Once completed, Ibrahim made a global call to pilgrimage (Hajj) from Mount Arafah, a call which Allah ensured was heard by people throughout history.
key_points: The Ka'bah was the first house of worship ever built for mankind.
Ismail was approximately 16 years old when he helped his father build the Ka'bah.
Al-Hajar al-Aswad turned black over time due to the sins of humanity.
Allah promised Ibrahim that his call to Hajj would reach all people.

chapters.title: The Corruption of Tawhid and Introduction of Shirk
chapters.summary: The pure monotheism (tawhid) established by Ibrahim lasted for centuries until a tribal conflict between Jurhum and Khuza'ah. After Khuza'ah took control, the well of Zamzam was buried and hidden by the retreating Jurhum. The leader of Khuza'ah, Amr ibn Luhayy, eventually traveled to Syria and brought back the idol Hubal, believing it could provide rain and protection. He forced the Arabs to worship idols and corrupted the Hajj rituals, introducing shirk into the talbiyah prayer and establishing the era of Jahiliyyah.
key_points: Khuza'ah defeated Jurhum, leading to the temporary loss of the Zamzam well.
Amr ibn Luhayy is credited with introducing idol worship to the Arabian Peninsula.
Hubal was the first major idol brought to Makkah from Sham.
The talbiyah was corrupted to include 'partners' that Allah supposedly owned.

chapters.title: The Moral Decline of Jahiliyyah
chapters.summary: The speaker concludes by describing the moral degradation of the pre-Islamic Arabs through the story of Isaf and Na'ilah. After committing indecency at the Ka'bah, they were turned to stone as a warning, yet later generations were misled into worshipping those very stones. This highlights the absurdity of Jahiliyyah, where people would even worship idols made of dates and then eat them when hungry. This historical context illustrates the magnitude of the transformation the Prophet ﷺ achieved in turning these people into the Sahabah.
key_points: Isaf and Na'ilah were two lovers turned to stone for immorality at the House of Allah.
Amr ibn Luhayy placed the stones of Isaf and Na'ilah at the Ka'bah for worship.
Arabs were instructed to take stones from Makkah for worship during travels.
The Sahabah later mocked their own past practice of worshipping and eating date figurines.

segments.translit: Al-hamdu lillahi rabbi al-alamin wa sallallahu wa sallama wa baraka ala nabiyyina muhammadin wa ala alihi wa sahbihi ajmain rabbi ishrah li sadri wa yassir li amri wa-uhlul uqdatan min lisani yafqahu qawli allahumma allimna ma yanfauna wa-anfa'na bima allamtana wa zidna ilmaEn Meaning: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may prayers, peace, and blessings be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and all of his companions. "O my Lord! Open for me my chest, and ease for me my task, and untie the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech." O Allah, teach us that which benefits us, and benefit us with that which You have taught us, and increase us in knowledge.

segments.text: [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]] tonight we will start with the biography of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, the [[Seerah|سيرة]] of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
And there are so many benefits in studying the life and the mission and the struggles of our beloved Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

And the fact that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] sent him as a messenger for this [[Ummah|أمة]], and Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] chose to send a man, a human being, instead of an angel.
It shows that we are required to emulate him and to follow his example.

Because if Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] had sent an angel as a messenger instead, then the human beings would say, "Okay, these are angels, they're able to do what we are not able to do."
But because Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] sent a messenger, we are required to follow him and we have no excuse not to follow him. And his example is the best example.
Surely you have in the Messenger of Allah a good example for those who desire Allah and the Last Day and those who remember Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] often.
So by studying the [[Seerah|سيرة]], the life of the Prophet ﷺ, we learn how to follow in his footsteps.
By knowing how he lived his life, we know how to live our life.
And another benefit in studying the [[Seerah|سيرة]] of the Prophet ﷺ is that it is something that acts as such a boost to your [[Iman|إيمان]].
When you read about the Prophet ﷺ and the different incidents in his life, the way he received revelation, the way he dealt with people, the way that he struggled for this [[Ummah|أمة]].
Just reading about his life, it just increases you in love for him. Nobody can read the [[Seerah|سيرة]] of the Prophet ﷺ and not increase in their love and respect for him.
And this even goes for people who are not Muslims.
Any non-Muslim who reads about the life of the Prophet ﷺ, [[Wallahi|والله]] they will not be able to read it except with an increase of respect and honor for him that they hold in their hearts.
And this is something that is easily visible. Even the non-Muslims who study about the life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, they have nothing but praise for him and respect for him.
So this is one of the great benefits of studying the [[Seerah|سيرة]] of the Prophet ﷺ, is that it increases our love for him.
And loving the Prophet ﷺ is part of our [[Iman|إيمان]].

segments.translit: La yu'minu ahadukum hatta akuna ahabba ilayhi min walidihi wa waladihi wa-nnasi ajmainen Meaning: None of you will have true, complete faith until he loves me more than he loves his father, his child, and all of mankind.

segments.text: None of you will have true, complete [[Iman|إيمان]] until he loves me more than he loves his father and his child and all of mankind.
So studying the [[Seerah|سيرة]], studying the life of the Prophet ﷺ, is one guaranteed way to increase in your love for the Prophet ﷺ.
Another great benefit of studying the [[Seerah|سيرة]] of the Prophet ﷺ and studying his life is that it helps you to understand the Quran.
The Quran is the word of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] as was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. But how do we see the Quran in practice?
How do we see the Quran actually being implemented?
We see it through the character of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. We see its implementation in the life of the Prophet ﷺ.
[[Aishah|عائشة]] was asked about the [[khuluq|خُلُق]] of the Prophet ﷺ. And then she answered them by saying "Don't you read the [[Quran|قُرْآن]]? Don't you read the [[Quran|قُرْآن]]?
Why do you need to ask me this question? If you read the [[Quran|قُرْآن]], you will know the answer to this question."
His character was the [[Quran|قُرْآن]]. So if you want to see the actual practical implementation of the [[Quran|قُرْآن]] in someone's life,
then you look at the life of the one to whom it was revealed, the Prophet [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ.
Another thing is that there are some [[ayat|آيَات]] in the [[Quran|قُرْآن]] that you will not be able to fully understand
unless you know the situation or the time in the life of the Prophet ﷺ that that [[ayat|آيَة]] was revealed.
For example, Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] says:

Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] revealed this [[ayat|آيَة]] to the Prophet ﷺ. [[innaka la tahdee man ahbabt|إِنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ]], surely you do not guide whom you love.
Surely you cannot guide the one whom you love. [[wa lakinna Allaha yahdee man yashau|وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ]], but Allah guides whomever He wills.
This is an [[ayat|آيَة]] and what I just said is the translation of that [[ayat|آيَة]].
But to fully, really comprehend the gravity of this [[ayat|آيَة]], you have to know what the situation was when it was revealed.
The uncle of the Prophet [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]]. [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] defended his nephew, the Prophet ﷺ, he defended him from harm.
[[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], he was one of the leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], he was a very powerful man.
So when anyone wanted to harm the Prophet [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ for his [[dawah|دَعْوَة]], [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] would be a shield in between that person and the Prophet ﷺ.
He would not let anyone touch his nephew, even though he didn't become a Muslim.
[[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] did not accept [[Islam|إِسْلَام]] because he didn't want it to be said about him that this person left the religion of his father and his grandfather.
He didn't want that to be said about him after he passed away. So he defended the Prophet ﷺ and he helped him a lot throughout his period in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
From when the Prophet ﷺ proclaimed his messengership in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] up to the end of the [[Makkiyah|مَكِّيَّة]] period when [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] died.
[[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] was a great help to the Prophet ﷺ. So of course, the Prophet ﷺ had this honor and had this love for his uncle.
First of all, he's his uncle, he's a blood relation, and secondly, he helped him so much.
Now when [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] was about to die, he was on his deathbed, the Prophet ﷺ said to him, "O my uncle, say [[la ilaha illa Allah|لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّه]]."
"Say [[la ilaha illa Allah|لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّه]]. Just give me something that I can intercede with Allah on your behalf on [[Yawm al-Qiyamah|يَوْم الْقِيَامَة]]."
"Just say these words and I will intercede on your behalf with Allah on [[Yawm al-Qiyamah|يَوْم الْقِيَامَة]]. Just say [[la ilaha illa Allah|لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّه]]."
But [[Abu Jahl|أَبُو جَهْل]] and some of the other [[kuffar|كُفَّار]] of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] were also present at the time.
And they said, "O [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], are you going to leave the religion of your father? Are you going to leave the religion of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]]?"
And then [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] died and the last thing that he said was, "I die on the religion of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]]," and he passed away.
So how do you think the Prophet ﷺ felt about that? Of course, it was very saddening to him.
It really, really caused him a lot of pain to see his uncle die in such a way, on disbelief.
And then Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] revealed this [[ayat|آيَة]]: "Surely you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills."
Now think about it. If you just know this [[ayat|آيَة]] without knowing the story behind it, without knowing the incident from the Prophet's ﷺ life behind it,
without knowing the relationship between [[Rasulullah|رَسُولُ اللَّهِ]] ﷺ and his uncle [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], if you don't know that whole backstory,
then you will not fully be able to comprehend the deepness of this [[ayat|آيَة]].
That's why it's important to study the [[Seerah|سِيرَة]] of the Prophet ﷺ, to study his life, to study his interactions with other people,
to study the different situations that happened in his lifetime. And only through this will you fully be able to understand the [[Quran|قُرْآن]].
So this is a very important benefit of [[Seerah|سِيرَة]] as well. And the [[ilm|عِلْم]], the knowledge of [[asbab al-nuzul|أَسْبَاب النُّزُول]],
the knowledge of the reasons for revelation, why were certain [[ayat|آيَات]] revealed.
revealed? What was the situation that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] chose to reveal these [[ayat|آيات]]?
This science of the reasons of revelation, it is part of the [[Seerah|سيرة]] of the Prophet ﷺ.
And when you study that, and when you understand that, it will give you a fuller and more comprehensive understanding of the Quran itself.
Now, many teachers, when they start teaching lessons about the [[Seerah|سيرة]] of the Prophet ﷺ, they may start with their starting point at the birth of the Prophet ﷺ.
But to really give a more comprehensive idea of the society that the Prophet ﷺ came into, it's important that we don't start at his birth, but we have to start before his birth.
To understand what type of a society it was that the Prophet ﷺ came into.
What was this society, the Meccan society that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] chose to send His Prophet ﷺ and start his mission from that place?
So we need to go back in history a little bit.
Before we start about the birth of the Prophet ﷺ and his youth, and his prophethood, and his mission, we will go back in history to the civilization of [[Makkah|مكة]].
We have to talk about the early beginnings of Meccan society and civilization in [[Makkah|مكة]].
And that traces back all the way to the time of [[Ibrahim|أبو الأنبياء]], the father of the prophets, [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].

And he is known as [[Ibrahim|أبو الأنبياء]], the father of the prophets, because all of the prophets who came after him, they came from his lineage, through his son [[Ishaq|إسحاق]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]],
except for the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, who came through the lineage of his other son, [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
So we need to go back to the beginning of the Meccan society.
Now, many of you are familiar of the story of why [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] went to [[Makkah|مكة]] in the first place.
[[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], originally he was from what is modern-day [[Iraq|العراق]], and then he went to [[Filastin|فلسطين]], that area in [[ash-Sham|الشام]].

And then Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] commanded him to go from [[Filastin|فلسطين]] to [[Makkah|مكة]], and to take his wife [[Hajar|هاجر]] and his son [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
He ordered him to take his wife and his son to [[Makkah|مكة]], go from [[Filastin|فلسطين]] to [[Makkah|مكة]]. So he took his wife and his son, baby, to [[Makkah|مكة]].
He left them in [[Makkah|مكة]], and he turned away and started going back.
So his wife [[Hajar|هاجر]], she said to him, "Why are you leaving us here?" And she started to follow him and ask him, "What are you doing?
How can you leave me and my son, our son here, like this?"
You know, there's no one here, there's nothing here. There was nothing there.
Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] describes [[Makkah|مكة]] as
It is a valley with no agriculture, no vegetation, no water, no nothing. No people, nothing. Just an empty, barren land.
So he left his wife and his baby son there, and he started to leave.
So she was surprised at this, like what's going on here? So she went and she followed him and she asked him, "Why are you leaving us here? What is this?"
But he didn't turn back to talk to her. He kept on. He didn't even turn back.
So then she understood, and she asked him,
"Did Allah order you to do this?" And then he replied in the affirmative, he said, "Yes."
So she said,
"If that is the case, then Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] will never cause any harm to come to us. Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] will definitely protect us."
She was comfortable with that. Once she heard that this was the order of Allah, she had peace in her heart and she felt that relaxation.
And that shows the strength of her [[tawakkul|توكل]] on Allah, her dependence upon Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
So [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] left them there, and he went back to [[Filastin|فلسطين]].
Now, as we mentioned, this land in [[Makkah|مكة]], no vegetation, no water, nothing, no people.
It was just [[Hajar|هاجر]] and her son [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
So the son, the baby, he became thirsty after some time. He needed some water to drink.
So she started going around looking for water. His mother started going around looking for water, from the mountain of [[Safa|الصفا]] to the mountain of [[Marwah|المروة]].
Back to [[Safa|الصفا]] again, back to [[Marwah|المروة]], looking anywhere for water. And she left her son in a certain place between those mountains.
And [[Jibril|جبريل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] came down, and he hit the earth with his wing, and the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] sprung forth.
So the [[Zamzam|زمزم]] water started gushing forth. And this was a blessing that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] gave to these people.
So it was a place that had no water, and now suddenly [[Jibril|جبريل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] comes, he hits the ground with his wing and the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]] springs out.
So now they have water to drink, blessed water, and they are able to quench their thirst, [[walhamdulillah|والحمد لله]].
Now, the Arabian Peninsula at that time, it was inhabited in places from different tribes.
But the original Arabs, the origin of the Arabs is not from different parts of the Arabian Peninsula, but it is from [[Yemen|اليمن]].
The original Arabs, they came from [[Yemen|اليمن]]. That's where the Arabs were first found, in Arab, in [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And they stayed there for a long time, and they had a water supply in [[Yemen|اليمن]]. They had a big water supply in [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And they built a dam to, you know, to get the water from the storms and the rain.
And that dam was called [[Sadd Ma'rib|سد مأرب]], the dam of [[Ma'rib|مأرب]].
And that was where the water supply used to come for them, so they used to drink from that water, and they built their civilization around that area.
Now, eventually something happened and that well was destroyed, so they lost that source of water. So that is why the Arabs, they left [[Yemen|اليمن]].
They were originally from [[Yemen|اليمن]], but once that water supply was gone, that's when they left [[Yemen|اليمن]].
That's when they left into different parts of the Arabian Peninsula in search for water, because there can be no civilization without water.
So they started moving around the Arabian Peninsula, looking for places where they could start a civilization, but they needed water for that.
So they would go here and there in different places looking for water.
So there was a tribe of the Arabs, they were called, the name of this tribe was [[Jurhum|جرهم]].
The name of this tribe was [[Jurhum|جرهم]], and they happened to be around the [[Makkah|مكة]] area.
They happened to be around the [[Makkah|مكة]] area, looking for a place where they could settle and find some water.
And while they were passing around [[Makkah|مكة]], they saw some birds. They saw some birds, and the birds, you know, were going in a certain direction.

So they thought to themselves, "There has to be water around here somewhere, because there's no way that there can be birds flying around this area except that there has to be water here, because birds need water too."
So they decided to investigate this. So they looked to where those birds were actually going, and they followed it, and they found [[Hajar|هاجر]] and [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
And they found that well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]], this tribe called [[Jurhum|جرهم]].
And they were honorable people, they were good people. They were people who were noble in their character.
So they could have, you know, it's just one woman and a baby, they could have easily, you know, took control and kicked them out or did whatever they want.
But they saw that, no, this well belongs to this woman and her son. "We don't have any right to take it without her permission."
So they asked for her permission. They said, "We would like to build our city around here. We would like to stay here, because there is water supply here.
But this is your water, but we would like to, you know, pay you a rent, so that we can use this water as well.
And we would like to stay here." So she said, "Okay, [[alhamdulillah|الحمد لله]]."
So they started paying her for the use of that [[Zamzam|زمزم]] water. So this was a source of [[rizq|رزق]] for her.
This was a source of provision for her and her son, [[alhamdulillah|الحمد لله]].
And they had their water as well, and the civilization started to flourish, [[walhamdulillah|والحمد لله]].
So [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] grew up in this kind of a society. He grew up amongst the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]].

Now, [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] and [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], they were not actually Arabs. They were not from [[Yemen|اليمن]], they were not from this place. They were not Arabs.
They came from [[Filastin|فلسطين]] area.
But when [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] settled in [[Makkah|مكة]], you know, he got married to a woman from the tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]] as well.
So the children of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] are known as Arabs who were, in Arabic they say [[musta'rab|مستعرب]], meaning they were not originally Arabs.
[[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] was not originally Arab, but he became an Arab by settling there, by marrying into the Arabs, and by living there in [[Makkah|مكة]].
And he learned Arabic. Arabic was not his language, but because he was born and brought up there in [[Makkah|مكة]] amongst the Arabs, this tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]], he learned Arabic as well.
So this was the beginning of civilization in [[Makkah|مكة]].
Now, [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], we said he went back to [[Filastin|فلسطين]], but he would come and
every so often and visit his son [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]. So he would come and visit every so often and then go back. Come every so often and go back.

And eventually Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala ordered him to go back to [[Makkah|مكة]] and to take his son [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] and to build a house of worship for the worship of Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala alone.

So [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] and his son [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], they built the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] in [[Makkah|مكة]] upon the foundations of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] that was originally built by [[Adam|آدم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
And the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] is the first house of worship that was built for the worship of Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, and it was built in the time of [[Adam|آدم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].

segments.ar: إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ
segments.translit: Inna awwala baytin wudi'a lin-nāsi lalladhī bi-Bakkata (3:96 Main Verse Fragment Routine Recitation Focus line text segment sample transcription formatting setup snippet focus). Exact context: 'Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Makkah...' [Surah Ali 'Imran: 96]. [Quran 3:96 snippet context]. Here text fragment recited: Inna awwala baytin wudi'a lin-nasi lalladhi bi-Bakkah ... Allah 'Azza wa Jal says it in Surah Ali 'Imran, verse 96.

segments.text: Surely the first place of worship for the worship of Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala alone, it was in [[Makkah|بكة]] or [[Makkah|مكة]].
And that was built by [[Adam|آدم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]. But eventually over time, that was destroyed, but the foundations remained.

So Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala commanded [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] with his son [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] to rebuild the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] upon the foundations of [[Adam|آدم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
And at this time when they were building the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], he was a teenager. He was around 16 years old.
So, you know, a young man helping his father build a house of worship for Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala alone.

So when he wanted to start the construction, [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] wanted to start building the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], he wanted a nice, strong stone to start the construction from the corner.
So he sent [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], 'Go find a good stone, you know, a good, strong stone that we can use to start this structure in the corner here.'
So [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] went around looking for a stone, but he didn't find anything that was appropriate for what his father wanted to do.
So he came back to tell his father, 'I couldn't find anything.' But when he came back, he saw that his father had the stone.
So he asked his father, 'Where did you get this stone?' And then he said, 'Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala sent it to us. This is from Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala.'
And that is [[al-Hajar al-Aswad|الحجر الأسود]]. That is what is now known as the Black Stone. But at that time it was not black, it was actually a white stone.
But over time, with the sins of the people, it became black.
So that's how they started the construction of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]. They put that stone in the corner, and they started building the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] layer by layer.
And [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], throughout the construction,
he had one stand that he would stand upon to look at the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] a little bit from the back during the phases of construction to make sure everything is straight,
to make sure nothing is getting crooked.
So he would take that elevated piece and he would take it a little bit far back, not so close to the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], but he would put it back.
And then he would stand upon it to look, to make sure that the construction is going properly and it's being built straight. And that is known as [[Maqam Ibrahim|مقام إبراهيم]],
the place where [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] stood. And he used to stand there to make sure that the construction was going properly.

segments.translit: Wa-ttakhidhū min maqāmi Ibrāhīma muṣallā [Surah Al-Baqarah 2:125 fragment]

segments.text: 'And take the [[Maqam Ibrahim|مقام]] - take the standing place of [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] as a place of prayer.'
And if you go to [[Makkah|مكة]] now, you will see the position of that [[Maqam Ibrahim|مقام إبراهيم]]. It's not so close to the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], it's a little bit far back
because [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] used that to see, to get a good view of the construction of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
Now once he finished building the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], then Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala gave him a command.
'Now call the people to make pilgrimage to this house.'
So [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], he was surprised. He said, 'I can call to it, I can call, but how are the people going to hear me?'
'Who is going to come? Who is going to hear me?'
'Surely the call is upon you - we are commanding you to make the call - but the reaching of that call to the people, that's upon us.
You don't worry about that. You just call and I will make sure that that call is heard.'
So [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], he goes to [[Arafat|عَرَفَات]] and he goes on [[Arafat|جبل عرفة]] and he makes the call to [[Hajj|حج]]. He calls the people to [[Hajj|حج]].
And Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala makes that call heard around the world, in the east and the west. Everybody hears it.
And they answer that call. They start answering that call, and people come from all over the place to make the [[Hajj|حج]], to make the pilgrimage to [[Makkah|مكة]].
And Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala put in the hearts of the people love for this house, love for the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
So people would come from everywhere and make the pilgrimage to the house of Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, worship Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala alone, and they would love this place.
Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala put that love of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] in the hearts of the people.

And through this, through the people coming from all over, making the [[Hajj|حج]], making the pilgrimage to the house of Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, the religion of [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] -
the pure monotheistic religion of [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] - it was spread in this way.
And Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala alone was worshipped in the [[Arabian Peninsula|الجزيرة العربية]].

There was complete [[tawhid|توحيد]] of the Arabs. Everybody worshipped Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala alone, and no one associated partners with Him. And this went on for many years, [[alhamdulillah|الحمد لله]].
Only [[tawhid|توحيد]] and no [[shirk|شرك]] in the [[Arabian Peninsula|الجزيرة العربية]].
After some time, as we mentioned, [[Jurhum|جرهم]] was the tribe that inhabited [[Makkah|مكة]].
Now there was another tribe called [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]].

And after some years, [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]] and [[Jurhum|جرهم]], they got into a fight, they got into a battle over who should have control of [[Makkah|مكة]], who should have authority of the house of Allah, and who should have authority over [[Makkah|مكة]].

So [[Jurhum|جرهم]] had been there for many years, since the time of [[Hajar|هاجر]] and [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], since [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] was a baby.
And this went on for many years, but then [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], they wanted to fight for that authority.
So these two tribes got into a battle, they got into a fight: [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]] and [[Jurhum|جرهم]].
And [[Jurhum|جرهم]] was defeated.
The tribe of [[Jurhum|جرهم]] was defeated, and the tribe of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], they took control and authority of [[Makkah|مكة]].
Now [[Jurhum|جرهم]], in the face of this defeat,
they realized that they were defeated and they had lost this battle, but they didn't want [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]] to be so happy with their victory. So what did they do?
They buried the well of [[Zamzam|زمزم]]. They buried the [[Zamzam|زمزم]].
And the reason why people had inhabited that area in the first place was because of the [[Zamzam|زمزم]], because of the water.
So what they did was they said, 'Okay, we don't have control anymore, but, you know, we're not going to make it so easy for them either.
We're going to bury this well. We're going to bury the [[Zamzam|زمزم]] spring.'
So they buried it. And no more [[Zamzam|زمزم]]. [[Zamzam|زمزم]] was gone.
So [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], now they had control of [[Makkah|مكة]], but they had no water supply anymore.
So they had to actually import water from the outside and bring it inside.
Now the leader of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]], he was a man named [['Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]].
[['Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]], he was the leader of the tribe of [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]]. So he became the leader of [[Makkah|مكة]].
And he was a man who was very well-respected by the people.
Nobody disobeyed him. If he said anything, the people would obey him immediately without question. It's like what he would say, that's the law. Everybody has to obey it.
So nobody thought about disobeying anything that this man said. He was well-respected, and everybody honored him.
Now, he traveled at one point in time, he traveled up to [[ash-Sham|شام]], the area of Syria and Palestine.
And when he was there, [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]], when he traveled there, he saw a group of people, a group of people called the [[Amaliq|عماليق]].
And he noticed that they had idols, stones that they used to worship besides Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].

They used to worship different stones. So [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]], as we mentioned, in the Arabian Peninsula, there was no [[shirk|شرك]]. Everyone worshiped Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] alone.
But when he went up there to [[ash-Sham|شام]], then he saw these people worshiping these stones and stuff. So he was surprised. He never saw anything like this before.
So he said, 'What are these things that you are worshiping? What is the purpose of this?'
They said, 'Yeah, these are, you know, these are our idols. When we're hungry, you know, they provide us with food.
When we are in a state of fear or we are oppressed, then they help us. When we are thirsty, when we don't have anything to drink, they provide us with water.'
So then he said, 'Oh, really?' He was surprised at this. So then he said, 'Can you give me one? Can I have one?
Because we have a water problem in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], you know.'
'There's no more [[Zamzam|زمزم]] anymore. We need water. We have to get water from outside. So you're saying that these things, if you pray to them, they'll give you water.
So can I have one? I'll take it back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and maybe we can get some water, too.' They said, 'Yeah, sure.'
They gave him an idol. They gave him an idol, and the name of this idol was [[Hubal|هبل]]. And he brought this idol back with him to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
This is the first idol that came into the Arabian Peninsula, the idol that was known as [[Hubal|هبل]].
So when he comes back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] with this idol in his hand, and as we mentioned before, [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]], he is a person who is obeyed by the people.
He comes back with this idol, and he tells the people...
comes back with this idol, and he tells the people: "Worship this idol."
And they obey him immediately. They start worshipping the idol.
And that is how [[shirk|شرك]] came back into the Arabian Peninsula.
There was no [[shirk|شرك]] in the Arabian Peninsula, and this is the man who brought it back: [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]].
So he orders the people to start worshipping this idol. They start worshipping the idol.
Over time, he brings more and more idols. He assigns one idol for each tribe. There are different tribes that are around, and he gives each tribe an idol.
So they start worshipping these idols at the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], at the House of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
And like we mentioned, the [[Hajj|حج]] had been going on from the time of [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[ʿalayhis-salām|عليه السلام]]'s call.
Now, it was still going on during the time of [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]], but he changed the [[talbiyah|تلبية]].
You know the [[talbiyah|تلبية]], and we still say it today:

segments.ar: لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ
segments.translit: Labbayka Allāhumma labbayk, labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk, inna al-ḥamda wan-niʿmata laka wal-mulk, lā sharīka lak.

segments.text: Now, he added a few words to this. At the end, he said:

segments.ar: لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ، إِلَّا شَرِيكًا هُوَ لَكَ، تَمْلِكُهُ وَمَا مَلَكَ
segments.translit: Lā sharīka laka illā sharīkan huwa lak, tamlikuhu wa-mā malak.

segments.text: At the end, he said: "[[lā sharīka lak|لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ]]: O Allah, You have no partner except for the partners that You have, but You own those partners and You own what those partners own."
So he said, yes, Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] is still the highest one, but He has certain partners, but He is the owner of what those partners own as well.
And he's talking about the idols here. So this is how he introduced [[shirk|شرك]]. Even into the call for [[Hajj|حج]], he introduced [[shirk|شرك]] into that as well.
And then he also said to the people: "If you are ever leaving [[Makkah|مكة]], if you ever have to go on a trip outside of [[Makkah|مكة]], you must take a stone with you from [[Makkah|مكة]]."
"You must take a stone with you from [[Makkah|مكة]], so that while you're outside of [[Makkah|مكة]], you worship that stone; you pray to that stone.
And when you are in [[Makkah|مكة]], you worship the idols that we have here in [[Makkah|مكة]]."
"But when you're out of [[Makkah|مكة]], you must take a stone with you and worship those stones." So this is how [[shirk|شرك]] was introduced into the Arabian Peninsula.
and they started worshipping the stones and calling upon idols besides Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], and the society deteriorated.
And before, when [[Jurhum|جرهم]] was still in control of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]],
There were a man and woman from [[Yemen|اليمن]]. The man's name was [[Isaf|إساف]], and the woman's name was [[Na'ilah|نائلة]], and they were in love with each other in [[Yemen|اليمن]].
So [[Isaf|إساف]] went to the father of [[Na'ilah|نائلة]] and proposed to her, asked for her hand in marriage, but the father of [[Na'ilah|نائلة]] refused, he rejected him.
So [[Isaf|إساف]] and [[Na'ilah|نائلة]], they were very sad about this. They really wanted to get married, so they made a plan.
They said, "Okay, look, everyone is going for [[Hajj|حج]]. Every year, people go and make this pilgrimage, so we will go for [[Hajj|حج]] as well."
"And when we're in [[Hajj|حج]], you know, there's so many people there, we can do whatever we want to do and nobody will know what's going on.
We can do it without anyone finding out."
So after this, the people, they started to lose their sense of [[tawhid|توحيد]].
So they made that plan, and they met each other in [[Makkah|مكة]] at [[Hajj|حج]], at the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], at the House of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
And they started worshipping these stones and calling upon idols besides Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], and the society deteriorated.
And they did an act of immorality and indecency right there at the House of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
They committed their [[fāḥishah|فاحشة]], they committed their immorality right there at the House of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
And before, when [[Jurhum|جرهم]] was still in control of [[Makkah|مكة]], there was a situation that happened.
So to punish them, Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] turned them into stones.
There were a man and woman from Yemen. The man's name was [[Isaf|إساف]], and the woman's name was [[Na'ilah|نائلة]], and they were in love with each other in Yemen.
He turned [[Isaf|إساف]] and [[Na'ilah|نائلة]] into stones. [[Isaf|إساف]] became a stone and [[Na'ilah|نائلة]], she became a stone as well.
So [[Isaf|إساف]] went to the father of [[Na'ilah|نائلة]] and proposed to her, asked for her hand in marriage, but the father of [[Na'ilah|نائلة]] refused; he rejected him.

So the people, what they did—and this was before [[shirk|شرك]] came into the Arabian Peninsula, this is still during the time of when [[Jurhum|جرهم]] was in charge, before [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]].
So [[Isaf|إساف]] and [[Na'ilah|نائلة]], they were very sad about this. They really wanted to get married. So they made a plan.

So what the people did with those stones, just so that people will have a reminder that this is what happens when you disobey and disrespect the House of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], this is what happens to you:
to serve as a reminder, they took the stone of [[Isaf|إساف]] and they put it on Mount [[Safa|صفا]], and they took the stone of [[Na'ilah|نائلة]] and they put it on [[Marwah|مروة]].

So the people would see these stones and they would remember what happened to these people and they would fear Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]]. They didn't worship those stones or anything.
But then when [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]] came and he introduced idol worship back into the Arabian Peninsula, what did he do? What do you think he did?
He took those stones—the stone on [[Safa|صفا]] and the stone on [[Marwah|مروة]]—and he put them back in front of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], and he told the people: "Worship these ones too."
So they started worshipping those stones as well. This is how [[shirk|شرك]] came into the Arabian Peninsula.
And it just gives you an idea of the society that the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, came into.
The reason I gave this whole introduction is so you know what kind of a society the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is being, you know, raised in.
Which type of society did Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] choose to send His final and His greatest messenger? This is the society.
And this type of attitude of these people, it lasted all the way up to the time of the Prophet ﷺ.
And how do we know that?
There's a [[ḥadīth|حديث]] of one of the companions, and he said that when they would leave [[Makkah|مكة]], if they would ever leave [[Makkah|مكة]], they would take the stone with them.
So it was still lasting up to the time right before the Prophet ﷺ.
What [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]], what he introduced, it was still going on up to the time of the advent of the Prophet ﷺ.
So one of the [[sahabah|صحابة]], he mentioned that when we would leave [[Makkah|مكة]], we would make sure we take a stone with us.
And if we could not find any stone, we would take some dates from [[Makkah|مكة]], and we would make those dates into some kind of a statue or something, a figure,
and we would worship those dates in place of stones instead.
So he mentioned, he said, like, "And you know, they realized it. After they became Muslims, they realized how ridiculous this was."
They said, "We would take those dates sometimes and make figurines or statues out of them, and when we were outside of [[Makkah|مكة]], we would worship that, we'd pray to it.
But then we would get hungry, and we would find nothing else to eat, so we would eat our god!"
"We would eat what we were just worshipping!" Just to show the ridiculousness of this type of a belief.
This is the [[Jahiliyyah|جاهلية]] society that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ came into.
And the reason why we gave this introduction is so you can see throughout the course, [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], how Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], through the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ,
how He turned these people from the worst of people to the greatest generation of people that mankind has ever seen: the [[sahabah|صحابة]], [[māshāʾAllāh|ما شاء الله]].
How Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] turned them around 180 degrees through His messenger Muhammad ﷺ.
And it's important to understand what kind of society it was so you can see the effect that the Prophet ﷺ had on that society.
And [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]] we will talk about that, and we will continue to talk about the effects of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his birth next week, [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]].

segments.ar: وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ، وَصَلَّى اللَّهُ وَسَلَّمَ وَبَارَكَ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ
segments.translit: Wa-Allāhu aʿlam, wa-ṣallallāhu wa-sallama wa-bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa-ʿalā ālihi wa-ṣaḥbihi ajmaʿīn.

review.q: Why is it important that the [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] was a human messenger rather than an angel?
review.a: Following a human messenger provides a practical and achievable example for believers to emulate. It removes the excuse that his level of obedience is impossible for mankind.

review.q: What is [[asbab al-nuzul|أَسْبَاب النُّزُول]] and why is it significant in studying the [[Seerah|سيرة]]?
review.a: It refers to the science of the reasons for revelation. It provides the historical context, such as the death of [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], necessary to understand the depth and gravity of certain Quranic verses.

review.q: Who were the [[Jurhum|جرهم]] and how did they become the first to settle [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]?
review.a: They were a noble tribe from [[Yemen|اليمن]] who were traveling nearby. They were attracted to the area after the miracle of the [[Zamzam|زمزم]] well was revealed to [[Hajar|هاجر]] and [[Ismail|إسماعيل]].

review.q: What is [[Maqam Ibrahim|مقام إبراهيم]] and what was its purpose during the construction of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]?
review.a: It is the station where [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] stood to oversee the construction work. He used it to ensure that the building was being built straight.

review.q: According to the speaker, why did [[al-Hajar al-Aswad|الحجر الأسود]] turn black?
review.a: The stone was sent from Allah and was originally white in color. It turned black over time due to the sins of humanity.

review.q: Who was [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]] and what was his role in the era of [[Jahiliyyah|جاهلية]]?
review.a: He was the leader of the [[Khuza'ah|خزاعة]] tribe who brought the first idol, [[Hubal|هبل]], from Syria to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. He is credited with introducing [[shirk|شرك]] and corrupting the pure monotheism established by [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]].

review.q: How was the [[talbiyah|تلبية]] prayer corrupted by the leaders of pre-Islamic [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]?
review.a: The prayer was changed from pure [[tawhid|توحيد]] to include the mention of partners. They added a phrase claiming that Allah owned these partners and everything they possessed.

review.q: What lesson does the speaker draw from the story of [[Isaf|إساف]] and [[Na'ilah|نائلة]]?
review.a: The story illustrates the absurdity and moral decline of [[Jahiliyyah|جاهلية]], where people eventually worshipped the very stones that were meant to be a warning against immorality. It highlights the massive transformation later achieved by the [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]].
